title: Annotatio V §.VIII reply (1): solace from presence not Oral alone; we dispute only corporal/oral-carnal
pass_a_gloss: I reply (1) It is well that the Author does not so far trust the Oral Eating of Christ’s body alone as to judge the juice of solace to depend on it — rather he fetches hither the true presence of Christ’s body and blood, and from this, and so from Christ’s body and blood themselves, derives every juice of solace; But wrongly, both here and elsewhere, above and below, he argues that the dispute between us is not about Oral Eating and that of the Unworthy alone, but also about presence itself and true Sacramental Eating — which thing we formerly committed to his Preceptor Danhauer to chastise: we are never and nowhere about to dispute with any of the Lutherans about the presence of Christ’s body, or about true sacramental Eating, namely the Spiritual — meantime forever to speak against both the Corporal and thence local and natural presence, and the Oral, and so far also natural and carnal Eating of Christ’s body, whether taught by a Lutheran or by any other whoever.
pass_b_english: Reply (1): good that he will not hang solace on Oral alone but fetches true presence — yet he wrongly says we also dispute presence and true sacramental (spiritual) eating.

As with Danhauer: we never dispute spiritual presence or spiritual sacramental eating with Lutherans; we forever oppose corporal/local/natural presence and oral/natural/carnal eating of Christ’s body.
source_text: Respondeo (1) Bene habet, quòd Autor soli Manducationi corporis Christi Orali in tantum non fidit, ut succum solatii ab ea dependere arbitretur, præsentiam potiùs veram corporis & sanguinis Christi huc arcessat, & ab hac, eóque ab ipso corpore & sanguine Christi succum solatii omnem derivet; Sed perperam, & hîc, & alibi, tùm suprâ, tùm infrà, non de sola Manducatione Orali & Indignorum, sed de ipsâ etiam præsentia, & vera Sacramentali Manducatione, nos inter disputari arguit; id quod retrò Præceptori suo Danhauer o castigandum commisimus, nunquam & nusquam de præsentia corporis Christi, vel de vera sacramentali Manducatione, Spiritualibus puta, cum quoquam Lutheranorum, disceptaturi, oblocuturi interim perpetuò tùm Corporali indeque locali & naturali præsentiæ, tùm Orali, eóque eatenus & naturali & carnali Manducationi corporis Christi, sive à Lutherano, sive ab alio quocunque doceatur.
